questions.question: What happens when a collision is detected in CSMA/CD?

answers.a: All stations stop transmitting and wait for a random backoff time
answers.b: The station that detected the collision continues transmitting
answers.c: The station that detected the collision stops and resends immediately

explanations.a: Correct! When a collision is detected, all stations stop and wait for a random backoff time before retransmitting.
explanations.b: Incorrect! All stations involved in the collision stop transmitting.
explanations.c: Incorrect! Immediate retransmission increases the chances of another collision.
explanations.d: Incorrect! Transmission resumes after the backoff period.

questions.question: How does the backoff algorithm in CSMA/CD help in collision resolution?

answers.a: It allows all stations to retransmit at the same time
answers.b: It ensures stations wait a fixed time before retransmitting
answers.c: It introduces a random delay before retransmission to reduce further collisions
answers.d: It prioritizes some stations over others to avoid collisions

explanations.a: Incorrect! If all stations retransmit at the same time, another collision occurs.
explanations.b: Incorrect! The waiting time is random, not fixed.
explanations.c: Correct! The random delay helps reduce the probability of repeated collisions.
explanations.d: Incorrect! CSMA/CD does not prioritize specific stations.

questions.question: Why does CSMA/CD use a backoff algorithm after a collision?

answers.b: To ensure devices transmit again at the same time
answers.c: To introduce a random delay and reduce repeated collisions
answers.d: To prioritize certain devices over others

questions.question: What determines the minimum packet size in Ethernet?

answers.a: The processing speed of the switches
answers.b: The propagation delay and collision detection requirements
answers.c: The total number of devices on the network
answers.d: The number of packets sent per second

questions.question: Which of the following best describes binary exponential backoff?

answers.a: A method to increase network bandwidth
answers.b: A way to ensure no device transmits data at the same time
answers.c: An algorithm that increases wait time exponentially after each collision
answers.d: A technique to detect hidden terminals in wireless networks
